topic: visual hierarchy in a simple event flyer
lesson: Hierarchy is easiest to learn by making one obvious focal point, then reducing everything else until the message reads in one glance.
next_practice: Design one flyer with a headline, a supporting line, and a call to action, then critique reading order and contrast.

topic: spacing and alignment in a one-page flyer
lesson: A clean grid and repeated alignment edge make the hierarchy feel stable; whitespace should separate groups without creating accidental gaps.
next_practice: Rebuild the flyer from run 001 with one repeated alignment edge, then compare how fast the page scans before and after tightening the spacing.

topic: type pairing basics in a small poster
lesson: A beginner pair works best when one font carries the voice in a short headline and a simpler font protects readability in the supporting text.
sources: Adobe Learn Pairing fonts like a pro
Google Design How to Choose a Web Font
Figma Guide to text in Figma Design
next_practice: Build a text-only poster using exactly two font families, then compare whether the headline still feels strong when the body font is kept plain.
